sources.note: RELATED LANGUAGE, NOT MINOKOK (Eastern = Labuk-Kinabatangan Kadazan [dtb], labu1249, Labuk River): Appendix 1, p. 120: 'Stress occurs on the penultimate syllable of a word. When suffixes and clitics are added to a stem the stress shifts from the penultimate syllable of the stem to the penultimate syllable of the new word.' Does not mention Minokok.

sources.citation: Banker, John and Elizabeth Banker. 1984. The Kadazan/Dusun language. In Julie K. King & John Wayne King (eds.), Languages of Sabah: A survey report, 297-324. Pacific Linguistics C-78. Canberra: Australian National University.
sources.note: Nothing. Intelligibility-testing survey; 'Minokok' is the ethnonym of the Sugut Kadazan test villages Moiwod KN and Entilibon KN (pp. 308-309); p. 324: 'The position of Minokok (as represented by Moiwod KN) has not yet been verified as to whether it is a part of the Sugut Kadazan dialect or distinct from it.'

sources.citation: King, Julie K. and John Wayne King (eds.). 1984. Languages of Sabah: A survey report. Pacific Linguistics C-78, vi+365 pp. (whole volume, incl. Smith, Kenneth D. 'The languages of Sabah: a tentative lexicostatistical classification', 1-49).
sources.note: Nothing: a full-text search for stress/accent/penult over the 368-page volume returns zero hits. Smith lists Minokok (MO: Moiwod KN, Entilibon KN, 96 PSC) as 'part of Inner Sugut Kadazan subdialect' of the Kadazan/Dusun language (pp. 37, 48).
